title: Perfect complex with residue-field degree-zero fibres
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme, let $K$ be a perfect object of $D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_S)$ [def-pc-derived-category, def-pc-perfect-complex], and let $u:\mathcal O_S\to K$ be a morphism in $D(\mathcal O_S)$. Assume that for every point $s\in S$ the map $\kappa(s)=H^0(\mathcal O_S\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{\mathcal O_S}\kappa(s))\to H^0(K\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{\mathcal O_S}\kappa(s))$ induced by $u$ is an isomorphism and $H^i(K\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{\mathcal O_S}\kappa(s))=0$ for all $i<0$. Then $H^0(u):\mathcal O_S\to H^0(K)$ is an isomorphism, and Zariski-locally on $S$ there is a decomposition $K\cong\mathcal O_S\oplus P$ in $D(\mathcal O_S)$, where $P$ is perfect of Tor-amplitude in $[1,\infty)$ [lem-pc-tor-amplitude-qcoh-test].

proof.text: At a point s, the degree-zero fibre of the structure sheaf has dimension one. The fibre isomorphism therefore gives beta_0(K,s)=1 by [lem-sc-derived-residue-unit-betti]. Negative fibre cohomology gives beta_i(K,s)=0 for i<0. Apply [lem-sc-perfect-finite-free-residue-model] to obtain an affine neighbourhood U and a bounded finite-free model B with B^i=0 for i<0 and B^0 free of rank one.

source.place: Tag 0E62, degree-zero fibre criterion, using the minimal model of Tag 0BCD

proof.text: Use the existing strictlyPerfect_single_restricted_unit helper in the module of [lem-sc-connective-rank-one-model-stalk] to establish strict perfection of the restricted structure-sheaf single complex. Represent the restricted arrow from the structure sheaf in degree zero to B by a chain map alpha using [lem-pc-perfect-affine-map-representative]. At every point x of U its degree-zero component is invertible on the stalk by [lem-sc-rank-one-residue-stalk-component], since the original fibre hypothesis holds at every x and B^0 is free of rank one throughout U. Stalks detect isomorphisms of module sheaves (the stalk criterion in the module of [lem-sc-flat-cover-module-isomorphism-reflection]); the over-site equivalence reflects them. Thus alpha^0 is an isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 0E62, residue-field unit argument with Tag 0BCD

proof.text: At the original point s, apply the same stalk component criterion. Exact localized stalks commute with derived homology by [lem-sc-localized-homology-stalk-comparison]. The source complex is supported in degree zero and the target has no negative terms. Its outgoing degree-zero differential vanishes because it kills the invertible component alpha^0. Consequently homology of the stalk chain map in degree zero is invertible. Naturality of the homology and restriction comparisons identifies it, up to conjugation by isomorphisms, with the stalk of H^0(u). This holds for every s, so the stalk criterion gives that H^0(u) is an isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 0E62, conclusion on H^0(u); exact restriction and homology

proof.text: Since alpha^0 is invertible, the chain-map equation saying that d_B^0 after alpha^0 is zero implies d_B^0=0. For the model transported to U, let p:B -> B^0[0] be the degree-zero projection and j its inclusion. The negative terms vanish and d_B^0=0, so these are chain maps and p after j is the identity on B^0[0]. Put N=ker(p), and factor the difference between the identity of B and j after p through this kernel to define the retraction B -> N. The resulting split short complex gives B isomorphic to B^0[0] direct-sum N. The terms N^i vanish for i<1: in degree zero the kernel inclusion has zero component and is monic, and in negative degrees N is a retract of the zero term of B. The isomorphism alpha^0 identifies B^0 with the structure sheaf.

source.place: Tag 0E62, local splitting, specialized to a rank-one degree-zero model

proof.text: Every term of N is a retract of a finite-free term of B, and N inherits its finite support. Restricting this termwise retraction again to the top open witnesses perfection directly from its definition. The terms of N are flat. By [lem-pc-bounded-above-flat-kflat], N is K-flat, so it computes derived tensor. Tensoring N, which vanishes below degree one, with any module sheaf in degree zero still vanishes below degree one, hence has zero cohomology there (the proved tensor bounds in WeilConjectures.Mathlib.Algebra.Homology.Monoidal). The open restriction comparison from [lem-pc-tor-amplitude-open-local] identifies the localized derived model with derived pullback to U. Applying Q to the chain splitting and its biproduct comparison gives the claimed derived splitting with the structure sheaf and Q(N).
